history.dynasty: Rebuilt in modern era (Swami Prabhanand Giri Maharaj)
history.period: CONFLICT: origins claimed 9th century vs 1735 CE (see summary)
history.summary: Maa Annapurna Temple in Sudama Nagar, Indore, is dedicated to Annapurna, the goddess of food and nourishment. Incredible India (official tourism) traces the site's origin to the 9th century, but another source dates a temple here to 1735 under Bajirao Peshwa I/Holkar patronage - the two origin claims conflict (verify); the visible complex is not from either period. The shrine was rebuilt in 1959 by Mahamandaleshwar Swami Prabhanand Giri Maharaj, who meditated under a banyan tree at the site from 1955; the new idol was installed on 22 February 1959. Its most recognisable feature, the grand entrance supported visually by four life-size elephants, was erected in 1975, and a new white Makrana marble temple within the complex was inaugurated on 3 February 2023. The architecture blends Indo-Aryan and Dravidian styles, evoking the Meenakshi Temple of Madurai, with shrines for Maa Kali, Maa Saraswati, Shiva, Hanuman and Kal Bhairav; it also runs the free Annapoorna schools for underprivileged children.

name: Annapurna Temple
town_description: Indore is the largest city and commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh, and was the capital of the Holkar dynasty under the Marathas. It blends historic landmarks like Rajwada palace and Lal Bagh Palace with a renowned food culture centred on Sarafa Bazaar. It has repeatedly been ranked India's cleanest city and is a major hub for education, trade, and tourism in central India.
